module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1180

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1180](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1180)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Sh02] Shparlinski, Igor E., *On a question of Erdős and Graham*. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2002),
  445-448.
- [Gl06] Glibichuk, A. A., *Combinatorial properties of sets of residues modulo a prime and the
  Erdős-Graham problem*. Mat. Zametki (2006), 384-395.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos1180

/--
`Represents ε p a s` says that the multiset `s` of denominators `n` with `1 ≤ n ≤ p^ε` and
`n` coprime to `p` has `∑ n⁻¹ = a` in `ZMod p`.
-/
def Represents (ε : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (a : ZMod p) (s : Multiset ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n ∈ s, 1 ≤ n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ ε ∧ n.Coprime p) ∧
    (s.map fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ZMod p)⁻¹).sum = a

/--
`C ε` is the least `C` such that, for all primes `p`, every residue modulo `p` is the sum of at
most `C` elements of `{n⁻¹ : 1 ≤ n ≤ p^ε}` (or `0` if no such `C` exists).
-/
noncomputable def C (ε : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {C | ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p, ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s}

/--
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist a constant $C_\epsilon$ such that, for all primes $p$, every
residue modulo $p$ is the sum of at most $C_\epsilon$ many elements of
$$\{ n^{-1} : 1\leq n\leq p^\epsilon\}$$
where $n^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $n$ modulo $p$?

The original question was answered in the affirmative by Shparlinski [Sh02], who proved that
$\ll \epsilon^{-3}$ summands suffice for all sufficiently large primes. This was improved to
$\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ by Glibichuk [Gl06]. It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$
summands are required, and it may be that $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$ is possible.

See also [540](https://www.erdosproblems.com/540).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1180.lean#L1249"]
theorem erdos_1180 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
    ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s := by
  sorry

/--
Shparlinski [Sh02] proved that $\ll \epsilon^{-3}$ summands suffice for every residue modulo
every sufficiently large prime, where the threshold on $p$ may depend on $\epsilon$. No bound
polynomial in $\epsilon^{-1}$ can hold for all primes, since when $p^\epsilon < 2$ the only
admissible denominator is $1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.shparlinski : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 3 ∧ Represents ε p a s := by
  sorry

/--
Glibichuk [Gl06] improved the bound to $\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ summands, again for every
sufficiently large prime.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.glibichuk : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 2 ∧ Represents ε p a s := by
  sorry

/-- It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$ summands are required. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.lower_bound : ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    K * ε⁻¹ ≤ C ε := by
  sorry

/-- Is $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.optimal : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    ∀ᶠ ε : ℝ in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0), (C ε : ℝ) ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1180

findings.description: The right-hand side bounds `C ε`. By definition `C ε` is the least C that works for ALL primes p. That is not the constant the source's remark is about, and with it the open question becomes provably false. If p is prime and p^ε < 2, the only admissible denominator is n = 1, so a Represents-multiset for the residue −1 consists of s.card copies of 1. That forces s.card ≡ −1 (mod p), so s.card ≥ p − 1. The set in `C` is nonempty for every ε > 0: that is exactly the right-hand side of `erdos_1180`, which is solved and has a formal proof. Hence C ε ≥ p − 1 for every prime p < 2^{1/ε}. By Bertrand's postulate this gives C ε ≥ 2^{⌊1/ε⌋−1}, which is exponential in 1/ε. Example: for ε = 1/10, p = 1021 < 2^10 gives C(1/10) ≥ 1020, while ε^{-(1+δ)} = 100 at δ = 1. So `∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] 0, C ε ≤ ε⁻¹^(1+δ)` is false, and the variant is settled with answer False for a trivial small-prime reason. The source leaves the question open. Lean checks, all using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound: (1) `(RHS of erdos_1180) → ¬ (RHS of optimal)`, in about 60 lines (the p^ε < 2 bound plus Nat.exists_prime_lt_and_le_two_mul, with ε = 1/m and δ = 1). (2) I inlined the linked plby formal proof of the main theorem, which compiles on this toolchain, and proved `¬ (type_of% @Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal)`. In other words, the theorem as elaborated (`answer(sorry)` becomes `True`) is refutable. The file itself notes the obstruction in the docstring of `variants.shparlinski`: "No bound polynomial in ε^{-1} can hold for all primes, since when p^ε < 2 the only admissible denominator is 1". `optimal` asks for exactly such a polynomial bound on the all-primes constant.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/1180 (LaTeX source, https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/1180): "The original question was answered in the affirmative, with $C_\epsilon \ll \epsilon^{-3}$, by Shparlinski \cite{Sh02}. This was improved to $\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ by Glibichuk \cite{Gl06}. It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$ summands are required, and it may be that $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$ is possible." In this paragraph C_ε is the constant for sufficiently large primes. The bounds it cites hold only in that regime; Glibichuk's abstract (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11006-006-0040-8) reads "Consider an arbitrary ε > 0 and a sufficiently large prime p > 2 ... N = 8([1/ε + 1/2] + 1)^2". An all-primes C_ε ≪ ε^{-3} would be false. The last clause poses an open possibility, not a trivially false one.
findings.suggested_fix:
Restrict to sufficiently large primes, as `variants.shparlinski` and `variants.glibichuk` already do:
```lean
theorem erdos_1180.variants.optimal : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    ∀ᶠ ε : ℝ in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0), ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ) ∧ Represents ε p a s
```
Alternatively, define `CLarge ε := sInf {C | ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p, ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s}` and bound `(CLarge ε : ℝ) ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ)`. Both forms typecheck, and the docstring should say that C_ε refers to all sufficiently large primes. The ∀δ/eventually encoding of ε^{-1-o(1)} is fine; only the constant needs to change.

findings.description: This variant uses the same all-primes `C ε`. `∃ K > 0, ∀ ε ∈ (0,1], K ε⁻¹ ≤ C ε` is true, but for a reason unrelated to the source's remark. As shown for `optimal`, small primes alone force C ε ≥ p − 1 for every prime p < 2^{1/ε}, which is exponential in 1/ε. So the statement would still hold even if every sufficiently large prime needed only O(1) summands. The source's "at least ≫ ε^{-1} summands are required" is the counting bound: sums of ≤ k inverses from ≤ p^ε denominators give at most (p^ε+1)^k residues. It sits in the same large-prime regime as "C_ε ≪ ε^{-3}" and "C_ε ≤ ε^{-1-o(1)}". The Lean statement follows from the source's claim but is much weaker. It is not false, so this is a modelling issue to fix together with `optimal`.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/1180: "... with $C_\epsilon \ll \epsilon^{-3}$, by Shparlinski ... improved to $\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ by Glibichuk. It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$ summands are required, and it may be that $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$ is possible." All of these statements refer to the large-prime constant.
findings.suggested_fix: State it for large primes: `∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 → ∀ P : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, P ≤ p ∧ p.Prime ∧ ∃ a : ZMod p, ∀ s : Multiset ℕ, Represents ε p a s → K * ε⁻¹ ≤ s.card`. Alternatively use `K * ε⁻¹ ≤ CLarge ε` with the large-prime constant proposed for `optimal`.

review.notes:
Scratch files are in /workspace/review.

- optimal_refute.lean: proves `(RHS of erdos_1180) → ¬(RHS of optimal)` using only the standard axioms.
- combined3.lean: inlines the plby proof (namespace renamed to Plby1180; it compiles on this repo's toolchain v4.33.1 with standard axioms only). It proves `¬ (type_of% @Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal)` unconditionally, and `plby_iff_fc`: the plby List-based statement is equivalent to the file's Multiset-based statement.
- fix.lean: the suggested replacement statements typecheck.

Other checks:
- `erdos_1180` (answer(True)) follows the site's wording: all primes, repetitions allowed via `Multiset`. Shparlinski and Glibichuk actually prove a stronger version, with pairwise distinct denominators and sufficiently large p. With distinct denominators, 'for all primes' would be false (p = 3, ε < log 2/log 3, residue 2). So the multiset reading is the one under which the site's recorded affirmative answer holds. The all-primes and large-primes existence questions are equivalent: finitely many small primes, each handled by at most p − 1 copies of 1⁻¹ = 1.
- The `formal_proof` link points to line 1249 of the plby file, which is the theorem. It proves an equivalent statement (List instead of Multiset; `0 < n` is definitionally `1 ≤ n`).
- Categories match the site: the problem is PROVED, and the ε^{-1-o(1)} question is open. The `optimal` defect is a statement problem, not a stale status.
- In `optimal`, encoding ε^{-1-o(1)} as `∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] 0, … ≤ ε⁻¹^(1+δ)` is correct; only the constant is wrong.
- The page's sentence "Croot proved that this is true using at most (log p)^{3+o(1)} many summands" is not formalized. That is an omission, not a defect.
- Definitions `Represents` and `C` match their docstrings. The `sInf ∅ = 0` junk value is never reached, because `erdos_1180` guarantees the set is nonempty.

demonstrated.claim: Taking the file's own `Erdos1180.erdos_1180` exactly as stated (via `type_of%`) as the only hypothesis, `Erdos1180Demo.optimal_as_stated_false` proves `¬ type_of% @Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal` using only standard axioms. `Erdos1180.C ε` ranges over all primes, and a prime p < 2^{1/ε} admits only the denominator 1, which forces C(1/m) ≥ p − 1 > m² = (1/ε)^{1+1} for a Bertrand prime m² + 1 < p < 2^m; so the right-hand side fails at δ = 1, and the 'open' question's answer is forced to be False.

The file's own main theorem `Erdos1180.erdos_1180` is the only hypothesis. It is tagged solved, and its linked plby Lean proof compiles on this toolchain, as I checked separately. That hypothesis makes `C ε` a true minimum. `card_ge` shows that if p^ε < 2 then only n = 1 is admissible, so representing −1 mod p takes at least p − 1 summands. `optimal_rhs_false` takes ε = 1/m, δ = 1 and a Bertrand prime m² + 1 < p < 2^m, which gives C(1/m) ≥ p − 1 > m², so the right-hand side copied from the file is false. `optimal_as_stated_false` then refutes the declaration exactly as elaborated, where `answer(sorry)` defaults to `True`. `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound: the file's sorried theorems enter only through their types.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«1180»

/-!
# `Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal` is settled by small primes

`Erdos1180.C ε` quantifies over *all* primes. If `p ^ ε < 2` the only admissible denominator is
`1`, so writing `-1 : ZMod p` needs `p - 1` summands. Hence `C ε ≥ p - 1` for every prime
`p < 2 ^ (1/ε)`, which is exponential in `1/ε`, so no bound `C ε ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ)` can hold as
`ε → 0⁺`. The only input is the file's own solved main theorem `Erdos1180.erdos_1180`, taken as
a hypothesis exactly as the file states it. That theorem has a linked Lean proof, and it makes
`C ε` a true minimum rather than the junk value `sInf ∅ = 0`.
-/

open Filter Topology

namespace Erdos1180Demo

/-- If `p ^ ε < 2`, every admissible denominator is `1`, so any representation of `-1 : ZMod p`
has at least `p - 1` summands. -/
theorem card_ge {ε : ℝ} {p : ℕ} (hp : (p : ℝ) ^ ε < 2) {s : Multiset ℕ}
    (hs : Erdos1180.Represents ε p (-1) s) : p ≤ s.card + 1 := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hs
  have hall : ∀ n ∈ s, n = 1 := fun n hn => by
    have h3 : (n : ℝ) < 2 := (h1 n hn).2.1.trans_lt hp
    have h4 : n < 2 := by exact_mod_cast h3
    have := (h1 n hn).1
    omega
  rw [Multiset.eq_replicate.mpr ⟨rfl, hall⟩] at h2
  simp only [Multiset.map_replicate, Nat.cast_one, ZMod.inv_one, Multiset.sum_replicate,
    nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one] at h2
  have h5 : ((s.card + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod p) = 0 := by push_cast; rw [h2]; ring
  exact Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.succ_pos _) ((ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff _ _).mp h5)

/-- Numeric helper: `2 (m^2 + 1) < 2^m` for `m ≥ 7`. -/
theorem two_pow_gt : ∀ m, 7 ≤ m → 2 * (m ^ 2 + 1) < 2 ^ m := by
  intro m hm
  induction m, hm using Nat.le_induction with
  | base => norm_num
  | succ k hk ih => rw [pow_succ 2 k]; nlinarith

/-- `Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal`: its right-hand side is FALSE, given the file's own
`Erdos1180.erdos_1180`. Take `δ = 1`, `ε = 1/m`, and a Bertrand prime `m^2 + 1 < p < 2^m`.
Then `p ^ ε < 2`, so `C ε ≥ p - 1 > m^2 = ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + 1)`. -/
theorem optimal_rhs_false (H : type_of% @Erdos1180.erdos_1180) :
    ¬ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ᶠ ε : ℝ in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0),
      (Erdos1180.C ε : ℝ) ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ) := by
  intro O
  have ht : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (m : ℝ)⁻¹) atTop (𝓝[>] 0) :=
    tendsto_inv_atTop_nhdsGT_zero.comp tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp (ht.eventually (O 1 one_pos))
  obtain ⟨m, hmN, hm7⟩ : ∃ m, N ≤ m ∧ 7 ≤ m := ⟨max N 7, le_max_left _ _, le_max_right _ _⟩
  have hC := hN m hmN  -- `C (1/m) ≤ (1/m)⁻¹ ^ (1 + 1) = m ^ 2`
  rw [inv_inv, one_add_one_eq_two, Real.rpow_two] at hC
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hlt, hle⟩ := Nat.exists_prime_lt_and_le_two_mul (m ^ 2 + 1) (Nat.succ_ne_zero _)
  have hm : (0 : ℝ) < m := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 0 < m)
  have h2 : (p : ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ)⁻¹ < 2 :=
    (Real.rpow_inv_lt_iff_of_pos (by positivity) (by norm_num) hm).mpr
      (by rw [Real.rpow_natCast]; exact_mod_cast hle.trans_lt (two_pow_gt m hm7))
  have hmem : ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod q, ∃ s : Multiset ℕ,
      s.card ≤ Erdos1180.C (m : ℝ)⁻¹ ∧ Erdos1180.Represents (m : ℝ)⁻¹ q a s :=
    Nat.sInf_mem (s := {C | ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod q, ∃ s : Multiset ℕ,
      s.card ≤ C ∧ Erdos1180.Represents (m : ℝ)⁻¹ q a s}) (H.mp trivial _ (inv_pos.mpr hm))
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hrep⟩ := hmem p hp (-1)
  have := card_ge h2 hrep
  have : Erdos1180.C (m : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ m ^ 2 := by exact_mod_cast hC
  omega

/-- `Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal`, exactly as the file elaborates it (`answer(sorry)`
defaults to `True`), is refuted by the file's own `Erdos1180.erdos_1180`. So small primes alone
force the "open" question's answer to be `False`. -/
theorem optimal_as_stated_false (H : type_of% @Erdos1180.erdos_1180) :
    ¬ type_of% @Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal :=
  fun O => optimal_rhs_false H (O.mp trivial)

end Erdos1180Demo

-- Only the standard axioms (no `sorryAx`): the file's theorems enter only through their types.
#print axioms Erdos1180Demo.optimal_as_stated_false

not_fixed.reason: Left alone on purpose. I flagged it only as questionable: it is true as written, just weaker than the source's large-prime remark. The rules say to leave questionable items alone, and the `optimal` fix does not force any change to it, because `C` is unchanged.

submission.summary:
I rewrote the right-hand side of `Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.optimal` so that it quantifies over sufficiently large primes, as `variants.shparlinski` and `variants.glibichuk` already do. It now reads `∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] 0, ∃ P, ∀ p ≥ P, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p, ∃ s, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ) ∧ Represents ε p a s`. The old version bounded the all-primes `C ε`. Every prime p < 2^{1/ε} admits only the denominator 1, which forces C ε ≥ p − 1, so the old statement was provably false and the open question was settled for a trivial reason. The ∀δ / eventually-as-ε→0⁺ encoding of ε^{-1-o(1)} and the `research open, AMS 11` tags are unchanged. The docstring now says that C_ε counts summands for sufficiently large primes, as in the Shparlinski and Glibichuk bounds, and why all primes fail. No other declaration changed; `C` is still used by `lower_bound`.

Checks:
- The edited file compiles with only the 5 `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
- A scratch proof (`/workspace/review/fixcheck.lean`) shows that the file's solved `variants.glibichuk` implies the corrected right-hand side for every δ > 1. So the new statement agrees with the known ε⁻² bound, and its open content is δ ∈ (0, 1].

Scratch files that import the module still see the old `optimal`: they load the prebuilt .olean, which I did not rebuild so as not to touch build artifacts in the checkout. The pre-existing `lakefile.toml`/`run/` changes are from the sandbox setup, not from me.

  sInf {C | ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p, ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s}

/--
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist a constant $C_\epsilon$ such that, for all primes $p$, every
residue modulo $p$ is the sum of at most $C_\epsilon$ many elements of
$$\{ n^{-1} : 1\leq n\leq p^\epsilon\}$$
where $n^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $n$ modulo $p$?

The original question was answered in the affirmative by Shparlinski [Sh02], who proved that
$\ll \epsilon^{-3}$ summands suffice for all sufficiently large primes. This was improved to
$\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ by Glibichuk [Gl06]. It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$
summands are required, and it may be that $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$ is possible.

See also [540](https://www.erdosproblems.com/540).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1180.lean#L1249"]
theorem erdos_1180 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
    ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s := by
  sorry

/--
Shparlinski [Sh02] proved that $\ll \epsilon^{-3}$ summands suffice for every residue modulo
every sufficiently large prime, where the threshold on $p$ may depend on $\epsilon$. No bound
polynomial in $\epsilon^{-1}$ can hold for all primes, since when $p^\epsilon < 2$ the only
admissible denominator is $1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.shparlinski : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 3 ∧ Represents ε p a s := by
  sorry

/--
Glibichuk [Gl06] improved the bound to $\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ summands, again for every
sufficiently large prime.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.glibichuk : ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 2 ∧ Represents ε p a s := by
  sorry

/-- It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$ summands are required. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.lower_bound : ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
    K * ε⁻¹ ≤ C ε := by
  sorry

/--
Is $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$? Here, as in the bounds of Shparlinski and Glibichuk,
$C_\epsilon$ counts the summands needed for all sufficiently large primes; the threshold may
depend on $\epsilon$. Over all primes the bound fails trivially, since when $p^\epsilon < 2$ the
only admissible denominator is $1$. Precisely: for every $\delta > 0$ and all sufficiently small
$\epsilon > 0$, is every residue modulo every sufficiently large prime $p$ the sum of at most
$\epsilon^{-1-\delta}$ elements of $\{n^{-1} : 1\leq n\leq p^\epsilon\}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1180.variants.optimal : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
    ∀ᶠ ε : ℝ in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0), ∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, P ≤ p → p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
      ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, (s.card : ℝ) ≤ ε⁻¹ ^ (1 + δ) ∧ Represents ε p a s := by
  sorry

end Erdos1180
